limits: Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed in the record; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.

Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.

Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.

Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.

name: m141_ddr2_sched
notes: Simulation and formal only (phase 0): the scheduler is checked against a behavioural DDR2 command-rule model written from the data sheet, and its rules are proved on its own command output. No PHY, no MIG, no board: the board items are hooks (planned) with the pre-registration in docs/memory_controller_plan.md section 12. "Latency" is clocks from the request handshake to the first data beat at the nexys_650 profile (tCK 3077 ps, CL 5).

item_views.title: Both policies, six traffic patterns, two timing profiles and three address maps against the behavioural DDR2 model: zero violations, every request served once, order kept, refresh gap within 9 x tREFI, longest wait within the bound
Sixteen seeded faults in a copy of the RTL (a timing constant short, the dependency check removed, refresh disabled, a wrong bank on the command bus, a wrong row opened) are each caught by the bench

SymbiYosys proofs of the timing rules and request order (k-induction with helper invariants, depth 3, at the real data sheet constants and at small ones, both policies), the refresh debt (property-directed reachability), covers, and one mutant per rule that a named assertion catches

requirements.text: For every request sequence and both policies, the command bus never breaks tRCD, tRP and tRPA, tRAS, tRC, tRRD, tFAW, tWR, tWTR, tRTP, tRFC, the read-to-write and write-to-read spacings, the one-command state rules (ACTIVATE to a closed bank, a column command to an open bank, REFRESH with every bank closed), nor the data-bus rules (no overlap, one idle clock between a read and a write burst).
requirements.title: No DDR2 timing rule is ever violated on the command stream

item_views.title: Median read latency, latency-first policy, light random reads

performance.condition: POLICY 0, random reads, mean gap 40 clocks, nexys_650 profile (tCK 3077 ps, CL 5), simulation, 3000 reads

requirements.text: Random reads at light load (one request every 40 clocks on average) find a precharged bank, so a read pays ACTIVATE, tRCD and the read latency and nothing else. The bound is a regression bound from the recorded run, not a target.
requirements.title: Median read latency of the latency-first policy on light random reads

item_views.title: 99.9th percentile read latency, latency-first policy, light random reads

performance.condition: POLICY 0, random reads, mean gap 40 clocks, REF_POST 4, nexys_650 profile, simulation, 3000 reads

requirements.text: The 99.9th percentile of the read latency at light load stays within a refresh's worth of the median (a refresh in progress when a read arrives is the tail). Regression bound, not a target.
requirements.title: Tail of the read latency of the latency-first policy on light random reads

item_views.title: Maximum read latency inside a refresh-deferral window, latency-first, REF_POST 4

performance.condition: POLICY 0, REF_POST 4, ref_defer high for 5000 of every 12000 clocks, random reads at light load, nexys_650 profile, simulation, 6000 reads
performance.quantity: maximum read latency inside the window

requirements.text: While ref_defer is high and the postponement allowance is not used up, refreshes that fall due are postponed, so the reads accepted in the window see no tRFC wait (the cost moves to reads after the window). Regression bound, not a target.
requirements.title: No read inside a refresh-deferral window waits for a refresh
